## Description

A ~10 µm unicellular green alga with two flagella that beat like a breaststroke, a large cup-shaped
chloroplast with a pyrenoid and an eyespot. With good light it doubles in ~6–8 h. It divides inside
the mother wall into 4 daughters (palintomy). Model organism for flagella, photosynthesis and
phototaxis.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `moss` (weight 0.2), `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15), `sea_ice` (weight 0.6); 150 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

Two-flagellum phototroph with [phototaxis](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md) and a
[photophobic response](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md): a sudden light increase makes it stop, swim
backwards briefly and leave in another direction. Helical swimming; 4 daughters per cycle
(`fissions_per_cycle`). Photobiont of the lichen fungus and host of chytrids.

## Literature

- Foster K.W., Smyth R.D. (1980) Light antennas in phototactic algae. Microbiol. Rev. 44: 572–630
  (photophobic response).
- Hegemann P. (2008) Algal sensory photoreceptors. Annu. Rev. Plant Biol. 59: 167–189.
- PNAS (1997): chlorophyll doubling ~20 h at ~70 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (not a cell count;
  temperature not verified).

## Not implemented yet

- No sexual cycle (gametes of + and − mating types, zygospore).
- The eyespot does not shade the photoreceptor; phototaxis compares light on both sides instead.
- Helix radius and period are estimates.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares the [phobic response](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md) with *Euglena* and *Blepharisma*,
[phototaxis](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md) with the flagellated phototrophs, and the
[lichen symbiosis](../../mechanics/symbioses.md#lichen) as a photobiont.
